title: Open scalar adjunction and the factored exceptional counit
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions, $m,n\ge1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$, and $\varphi:A\to B$ any unital map [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each scheme $T$ use constant module sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and write $S_T^{A,B}K=K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$ for uncompleted derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The notation $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$; all scheme maps are $k$-maps [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constructible exceptional functors and their adjunctions on bounded constructible inputs of etale origin [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and ordinary derived direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let $h:W\hookrightarrow X$ be factored as $W\xrightarrow{t}V\xrightarrow{j}X$, with $t$ closed and $j$ open. For each $R=A,B$, compact-support composition [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] identifies $Rh_{!,R}=j_{!,R}t_{*,R}$ on bounded-below etale-origin inputs; both intermediate compact-support operations preserve that class. The adjunction is the composite $j_{!,R}t_{*,R}\dashv Rt_R^!j_R^*$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], so $Rh_R^!=Rt_R^!j_R^*$ on bounded constructible inputs, with
$$\epsilon_{h,R}=\epsilon_{j,R}\circ j_{!,R}(\epsilon_{t,R}).$$
In particular these are the constructible exceptional functor and its actual counit, and for $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$, $j_R^*M$ and $Rt_R^!j_R^*M$ belong to their respective finite-Tor constructible domains.

Write $V_T=\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}$ for exact restriction of scalars. On the entire ordinary derived categories [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], $S_T\dashv V_T$ and $j_A^*V_X=V_Vj_B^*$ canonically. The composite of these adjunctions with $j_!\dashv j^*$ [prop-exc-open-adjoint] determines a natural $B$-linear isomorphism
$$e_{j,Q}:S_Xj_{!,A}Q\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}S_VQ\qquad(Q\in D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)),$$
normalized by the scalar unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ on flat-term K-flat models. For the canonical open restriction comparison $r_{j,M}:S_Vj_A^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*S_XM$, one has, for every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$,
$$\epsilon_{j,B,S_XM}\,j_{!,B}(r_{j,M})\,e_{j,j_A^*M}=S_X(\epsilon_{j,A,M}).$$
This equality holds in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ for the actual scalar and open adjunctions. No coefficient flatness is imposed.

proof.text: First fix either coefficient ring $R$. The schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and the complementary opens of closed immersions are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. For $t$, choose the compactification $(\mathrm{id}_W,t)$ in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Its compact-support functor is $Rt_*$, which is termwise $t_*$ by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact]. For $j$, choose $(j,\mathrm{id}_X)$, giving $Rj_!=j_!$. Apply [thm-sf-comp-composition] with $f=t$, $g=j$: it gives $Rh_!\cong j_!t_*$ and explicitly says that each compact-support functor preserves bounded-below etale origin. These assertions are used on that class only.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, open restriction and exceptional-counit compatibility; agent expansion using the Stacks adjunction formulas

proof.text: Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$. Restrict its finitely many constructible strata to $V$; restriction of a locally constant finite module sheaf remains locally constant finite. The exact inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies cohomology after restriction, so $j_R^*M$ is bounded constructible. To check finite Tor amplitude, take a bounded flat model of $M$ in an interval $[a,b]$ by [lem-sf-flat-model]. Its open pullback is again flat termwise and K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], stays zero outside $[a,b]$, and represents $j_R^*M$ by exactness. The converse of [lem-sf-flat-model] gives the same Tor interval. Now [thm-sf-preservation-class], applied to the separated finite-type map $t:W\to V$ over $k$, puts $Rt_R^!j_R^*M$ in $D^b_{ctf}(W,R)$. Both objects have bounded constructible etale origins by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. This reasoning is applied separately over $A$ and $B$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, open restriction and exceptional-counit compatibility; agent expansion using the Stacks adjunction formulas

proof.text:
For $H$ of bounded-below etale origin on $W$ and bounded constructible $M$ on $X$, the actual open adjunction [prop-exc-open-adjoint] and the relative exceptional adjunction [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!t_*H,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(t_*H,j^*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,Rt^!j^*M).$$
The first step's preservation assertion makes both Hom calculations legitimate. The actual constructible $Rh^!M$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] represents the same Hom functor. Both representing objects are bounded constructible by [thm-sf-preservation-class] and the preceding step, hence of etale origin. On this full category the unique counit-compatible right-adjoint isomorphism [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identifies $Rh^!$ with $Rt^!j^*$. By the definition of composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the composite Hom bijection has counit $\epsilon_j\circ j_!(\epsilon_t)$, and the uniqueness identification carries it to the actual counit of $Rh^!$. This proves the factored assertion without positing a general unbounded exceptional adjoint.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, open restriction and exceptional-counit compatibility; agent expansion using the Stacks adjunction formulas

proof.text: For the remaining steps work on the entire ordinary derived categories. Write $U_R=j_R^*$ and $J_R=j_{!,R}$. The exact scalar restrictions $V_T$ and the adjunctions $S_T\dashv V_T$ with unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ are supplied by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. The identified constant-ring pullbacks satisfy $U_AV_X\cong V_VU_B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], applied to $j$ and the compatible constant maps $A_T\to B_T$. Its inverse is the same action identification in the opposite direction. The normalized balancing comparison of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] gives the invertible scalar mate $r:S_VU_A\to U_BS_X$. In its left-tensor convention $1\otimes x$ is $x\otimes1$ after the symmetry for commutative rings; all maps retain the $B$-action. Thus $r$ is precisely the canonical open restriction comparison in the statement, including its scalar-unit normalization.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, open restriction and exceptional-counit compatibility; agent expansion using the Stacks adjunction formulas

proof.text:
The two composite adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] have left sides $S_XJ_A$ and $J_BS_V$, with right sides $U_AV_X$ and $V_VU_B$. Their Hom bijections, for any $Q\in D(V,A)$ and $H\in D(X,B)$, are
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_XJ_AQ,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(J_AQ,V_XH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,U_AV_XH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,V_VU_BH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_VQ,U_BH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(J_BS_VQ,H).$$
Here the scalar bijections are [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the open ones are [prop-exc-open-adjoint], and the middle identification is [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to these composite adjunctions and that specified right-adjoint isomorphism. It gives a natural isomorphism $e:S_XJ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BS_V$. It is a morphism in the $B$-module derived category, so its components are $B$-linear. The composite units use the specified scalar unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; this fixes the normalization, rather than merely choosing an isomorphism of the endpoints.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, open restriction and exceptional-counit compatibility; agent expansion using the Stacks adjunction formulas

proof.text:
Let $u_A:\mathrm{id}\to U_AJ_A$ be the actual open unit. The inverse $d_Q=e_Q^{-1}:J_BS_VQ\to S_XJ_AQ$ is normalized by its open transpose
$$S_VQ\xrightarrow{S_V(u_{A,Q})}S_VU_AJ_AQ\xrightarrow{r_{J_AQ}}U_BS_XJ_AQ.$$
This is exactly the inverse-transpose assertion of [lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization], with its $\lambda_j^{-1}=r$ and its common-right-adjoint comparison equal to the one just constructed by uniqueness. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] the displayed assertion says explicitly
$$d_Q=\epsilon_{j,B,S_XJ_AQ}\circ J_B\bigl(r_{J_AQ}\circ S_V(u_{A,Q})\bigr).$$
That cited result applies to finite commutative rings and arbitrary derived $Q$ without flatness or boundedness; therefore so does this formula.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, open restriction and exceptional-counit compatibility; agent expansion using the Stacks adjunction formulas

proof.text:
Take $Q=U_AM$. Substitute the formula for $d$ and use naturality first of $\epsilon_{j,B}$ and then of $r$:
$$\begin{aligned}
S_X(\epsilon_{j,A,M})d_{U_AM}
&=\epsilon_{j,B,S_XM}\,J_B\bigl(U_BS_X(\epsilon_{j,A,M})\,r_{J_AU_AM}\,S_V(u_{A,U_AM})\bigr)\\
&=\epsilon_{j,B,S_XM}\,J_B\bigl(r_M\,S_V(U_A(\epsilon_{j,A,M})\,u_{A,U_AM})\bigr)\\
&=\epsilon_{j,B,S_XM}\,J_B(r_M).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the right triangle identity $U_A(\epsilon_{j,A,M})u_{A,U_AM}=\mathrm{id}_{U_AM}$ for the actual open adjunction; the unit/counit identities are as in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity]. Precompose with $e_{U_AM}$ and cancel $d_{U_AM}e_{U_AM}=\mathrm{id}$. This is precisely
$$\epsilon_{j,B,S_XM}\,j_{!,B}(r_{j,M})\,e_{j,j_A^*M}=S_X(\epsilon_{j,A,M}).$$
All these are equations in $D(X,B)$, for arbitrary $M\in D(X,A)$; no coefficient flatness or exceptional-functor domain is needed here.
